page: Amazon Web Services r5d.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, tailored for high-memory enterprise applications requiring fast local scratch storage. It features 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 384 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance includes 1,800 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, while GPU hardware is not present.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable middle-tier parallel execution alongside modest single-threaded throughput. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench (1,152.0) and stress-ng (1,379.39), fall into the lower quartile, whereas multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core (40,666.75) and Geekbench multi-core (10,626.0) reach mid-range percentiles. Memory bandwidth yields 108.09 GB/sec for uncached read-only transfers and 47.91 GB/sec for write operations. In application-focused metrics, the instance achieves 38.57 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database score of 15,530.87, and static web serving throughput of 27.91 GB/sec.

From an efficiency perspective, the r5d.12xlarge delivers solid density for memory-bound systems that also benefit from onboard high-speed storage, removing the latency and separate overhead of network-attached volumes for temporary caching. The primary operational tradeoff lies in its single-thread compute limitations, making it less suitable for compute-bound pipelines with low thread counts. Consequently, the instance is well suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, distributed data processing, ETL workloads, and relational database systems with substantial working sets.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with 384 GB of DDR4 RAM at 3 GHz, 1,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark evaluations position its multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and transactional database performance within the middle 50% tier, achieving 38.57 million Redis SET operations per second and 108.09 GB/sec in large-block read throughput, though single-core performance remains in the lower quartile. Combining high memory density with fast local NVMe storage, this instance is suitable for in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, real-time analytics, and high-throughput data processing workloads.
